newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: AUK Corp, three other IPOs start trading.
newsitem.headline: AUK Corp, three other IPOs start trading.

text.p: South Korea's AUK Corp, Hyundai Housing and Industrial Development Co, and two other companies have begun trading for the first time, the Korea Stock Exchange said on Wednesday.
Dong Yang Elevator Co and Korea Electronic Terminal Co also began trading, the exchange said.

The base price of terminal maker AUK's 500,000 shares was set at 75,000 won per share, the highest base price set for an initial public offering. It ties the record set by DI Corp in July. AUK's initial public offering had been set at 15,000 won.
The base price is the weighted average of bids and offers received by the exchange and sets the trading range for the first day.
Hyundai Housing, a unit of the Hyundai Group, saw 6.2 million shares start trading at 17,000 won. Its IPO had been set at 15,000.
Dong Yang Elevator's 600,000 shares started trading at 35,000 won, against an initial public offer price of 22,000 won.
Korea Electronic Terminal saw 280,000 shares trade at 60,000 won. Its IPO had been set at 36,000.
